models.title: Model Comparison
findings: 30 models were evaluated using leave-one-litter-out cross-validation.
The best model is "each gene nudged independently, p=0.14" (cv_ll = -5844.4), outperforming the CLAIM baseline by 252.7 log-likelihood units.
5 model(s) outperform CLAIM; 23 perform worse.
13 of 30 models assign zero probability to at least one observed child, ruling them out as exact explanations.
The total spread from best to worst is 4689 log-likelihood units, indicating strong discriminating power in the data.

anomalies.title: Anomaly Scores
findings: Anomaly scores were computed for all 692 children under the CLAIM model.
Mean log-likelihood per child: -7.89 (std: 2.88).
No children were flagged as strong anomalies (none exceeded 2 std below the mean).
Litter with lowest average score: Hive1 (-9.13). Highest: Hive11 (-6.74).

mi_matrix.title: Mutual Information
findings: Mutual information was measured between 8 parent gene variables and 4 child traits (32 pairs).
Diagonal entries (same-trait parent-to-child) show very strong information transfer (mean z-score: 119.8), confirming that parent genes predict child traits.

24 of 24 off-diagonal pairs show high mutual information (z > 10). Strongest: A_size->sweet (z=1311), A_color->sweet (z=310), A_sweet->color (z=223). This cross-trait signal likely reflects correlated gene values across parents in the dataset rather than a coupled inheritance mechanism.

residuals.title: Residual Analysis
findings: Residuals were computed for all 692 children across 4 traits.

Per-trait average absolute residuals: color: mean |residual| = 90, median = 59; sweet: mean |residual| = 82, median = 9; size: mean |residual| = 62, median = 20; length: mean |residual| = 71, median = 85.
Sibling within-litter correlations: 1 of 56 trait-litter pairs are significant at p < 0.05 (mean |r| = 0.109).
The near-absence of sibling correlations is consistent with independent inheritance per child (coin-flip mechanism).
Trait co-occurrence: 94% of extreme values are same-trait (137 of 145), confirming traits vary independently.

r_sweep.title: Parameter Sensitivity (R Sweep)
findings: The nudge-range parameter R was swept from 50 to 300 (51 values).
Optimal R = 150 (cv_ll = -6097.1).
The curve shows meaningful sensitivity near the optimum (767.9 unit spread over R +/- 20).
Total range from worst to best: 4532 log-likelihood units, confirming that R matters and is well-identified by the data.

distribution_tests.title: Distribution Tests
findings: KS and AD goodness-of-fit tests were run on 56 litter-trait pairs (14 litters x 4 traits), comparing observed vs. simulated distributions.
12 of 56 pairs (21%) are significant after FDR correction (KS test).
Affected traits: color (10), length (1), sweet (1).
Affected litters: Hive1, Hive11, Hive1a, Hive1b, Hive2, Hive4, Hive5, Hive6, Hive7, Hive8.

The majority of litter-trait pairs pass the goodness-of-fit test, indicating the model fits most of the data well. The failures may point to systematic deviations in specific traits or litters worth investigating.

mixture.title: Mixture Decomposition
findings: A CLAIM + INDEP mixture model was fitted to each of 14 litters via EM.
Mean CLAIM weight across litters: 0.9990 (range: 0.9990 to 0.9990).

All litters assign >= 95% weight to CLAIM, with INDEP contributing negligibly. This confirms that virtually all offspring are well-explained by the CLAIM mechanism and there is no evidence of a secondary independent-assignment process.
Adding the INDEP component changes mean log-likelihood by -0.05 per litter, providing no meaningful improvement over pure CLAIM.
